criterion_assessments.criterion: Separate every assigned source fact from proposed assumptions and established derivations.
criterion_assessments.evidence: The packet facts are labeled separately. P1 supplies a proposed uniform clock; P2 supplies a proposed discrete velocity definition. Each derivation states its premises and conditional scope.

criterion_assessments.criterion: Explain why position-versus-index alone does not determine speed or c.
criterion_assessments.evidence: A dimensionless index leaves delta x=L with length units and no time denominator. The alternatives tau and 2 tau preserve x(n) but change a nonzero step ratio, establishing non-identifiability.

criterion_assessments.criterion: Give a dimensionally consistent conditional proposal, such as t(n)=n tau with tau>0 and v=L/tau, without claiming that clock rule is assigned.
criterion_assessments.evidence: Under the explicitly unassigned t(n)=n tau, tau>0 and [tau]=time, delta t=tau, so v=L/tau has length/time units. The speed magnitude is abs(L)/tau; the discrete ratio does not prove an interpolated instantaneous speed.

criterion_assessments.criterion: State what evidence or definition would be needed to identify v with c; make no validated physics or Aether-Flow result claim.
criterion_assessments.evidence: The candidate requires a definition of c, physical interpretation and independent clock calibration or constraining law/measurement. Choosing tau=L/c is identified as imposed rather than derived. No validated physics or Aether-Flow claim appears.
